newsitem.title: ITALY: Virgin Express expects to have Boeing fleet.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Express expects to have Boeing fleet.

text.p: New European airline Virgin Express expects to build its fleet around aircraft supplied by U.S. manufacturer Boeing, chief executive Jonathan Ornstein said on Monday.
"I've held talks with Airbus, McDonnell Douglas and Boeing...at this point the Boeing aircraft seem to make sense," Ornstein told Reuters in an interview.
He said the company at present ran 14 Boeing aircraft and expected to have 20 by the end of 1997.
Virgin Express currently holds five year, staggered leases on its aircraft. Ornstein said that as these leases expired he hoped to replace them with leases for Boeing 737-700s.
British entrepreneur Richard Branson launched the Brussels-based Virgin Express in April after buying 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines SA (EBA).

The company forms part of the private Virgin group, which includes Virgin Atlantic Airways and package holiday and cargo affiliates in the Virgin Travel Group. -- Crispian Balmer, Rome newsroom +396 6782501
